we propose a novel NAS framework that can rapidly search for an optimal neural architecture for a given dataset.
we propose an efficient Neural Architecture Search framework that is trained on a database of datasets and architectures and can rapidly search the architecture for a given novel dataset.

we propose MetaD2A, a novel meta-learning framework that learns a latent space between datasets and architectures, and that MetaD2A achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple tasks with a rapid search time of 0.33 GPU second per task.

this paper proposes a meta-learned neural architecture search (NAS) model that can search for the neural architecture for a target dataset in a rapid and efficient way.

this work is an attempt to use the knowledge of existing datasets and pretrained models to accelerate the process of searching for the best neural network for a new dataset, by training the MetaD2ANet model on the dataset-to-architecture mapping of the existing datasets and pretrained networks, and then using the model to search for the best neural architecture for the new dataset.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a meta-learning based framework for neural architecture search, which can rapidly generate neural architectures for unseen tasks (datasets) from a dataset of tasks (datasets).
our model can rapidly generate a neural architecture for an unseen task (dataset) with a few-shot learning.
our model can learn the mapping between a given set (a dataset) and a graph (a neural architecture).

the proposed MetaD2As framework enables us to efficiently search for a neural network architecture for a novel task by leveraging the knowledge from the databases of datasets and pretrained architectures, and thus, we believe that our work opens up new research directions for rapid NAS as a well as ways to use the knowledge from the accumulated databases of datasets and pre-trained architectures.
